title: Anonymous retained MQTT publishes fill an unbounded in-memory retainMessages map
source: MQTT PUBLISH with retain=true, attacker-controlled distinct topicName and payload
driver: distinct retained topic cardinality and retained payload bytes up to the configured MQTT frame limit
retention: retained messages stay in the process-level retainMessages map until overwritten by the same topic or process restart; no eviction, TTL, byte quota, or topic quota found
bound: default messageMaxSize 4194304 caps one MQTT frame and therefore one retained payload, but total retained count and aggregate bytes are unbounded; default auth and ACL allow publish
impact: few hundred 4MiB retained messages can plausibly exhaust a small/default broker heap. Static-only run did not measure heap or service failure threshold.
static_trigger_shape: CONNECT anonymously, then publish retained messages to topics like dos/retain/{i} with payloads near the default 4MiB frame cap or many small payloads for key cardinality.
scope_notes: Default MQTT broker feature; not disk persistence.
